channel.title: AI GridWatch — California data center updates
channel.description: Data center moratoriums, proposals, and community-impact headlines for California, from AI GridWatch.

item.title: Tulare County: data center moratorium — Enacted
item.description: 45-day moratorium (extendable to 10 mo 15 days) on new data center applications in unincorporated areas

item.title: Monterey Park: data center moratorium — Enacted
item.description: Permanent ban via ballot measure, approved overwhelmingly by voters — first U.S. city to ban data centers by popular vote. Originally a 45-day moratorium (Jan 21), extended 1 year, then put on the ballot

item.title: Coachella: data center moratorium — Enacted
item.description: 45-day moratorium on new data-center applications, adopted unanimously alongside terminating the city's agreement with Stronghold Power over a 400+-acre, six-data-center campus; extended Jul 9, 2026 as the council moves toward a permanent ban. Treat any specific expiry as unconfirmed — the council was actively extending it as of this writing.

item.title: Imperial County: data center moratorium — Enacted
item.description: 45-day urgency ordinance, extended unanimously on Jul 14 by 10 months 15 days — a full year of paused permits while an advisory committee drafts rules (recommendations due Jan 2027)

item.title: Desert Hot Springs: data center moratorium — Enacted
item.description: 45-day urgency ordinance extended unanimously on Jul 7 by 22 months 15 days — the full two years California law allows
